transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 37 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jamie (Aurora Lead Eng), Carlos (Aurora Product), Lina (Aurora Security), Priya (Aurora SRE)

Summary: quick sync on POC progress, review of structured output integration via Redwood SDK, tuning notes for latency/cost, security questions around KMS and audit logs, agree next steps and owners.

00:00 Maya: all right everyone, thanks for joining uh today's the weekly POC sync. quick roll call — I think we have the usual group?
00:08 Jamie: yep here, Jamie — quick status, we ran the batch tests last night.
00:12 Ethan: nice, do you have the latency numbers handy?
00:15 Jamie: uh yeah so rough numbers — hosted run was about 420ms p95 for the long prompt set, dedicated quantized (4-bit) was down to about 160ms p95 but token costing was higher until we tuned batching.
00:28 Carlos: wait that 420ms was hosted? for our longer clinical notes prompts?
00:31 Jamie: yeah, long sequences 1k tokens, the hosted endpoint we used out of the box — think you guys called it Redwood Hosted API — gave ~420ms p95, but we saw a lot of variability during the midday test window.
00:45 Ethan: that's expected — routing and multi-tenant bursts can cause variance. for consistent p95 we'd recommend dedicated or pinning a model variant; also enable prefix KV cache for the parts of the note that are repeated.
00:56 Lina: quick security Q — when you say dedicated, is that the one in our VPC or the managed dedicated pool? we need to know data egress and KMS boundaries.
01:04 Maya: good question. for the pilot we gave you Dedicated reserved capacity in our shared zone but we can move to your VPC private deployment for full isolation. KMS can be customer-managed HSM or our integrated KMS — depends on your compliance needs.
01:17 Lina: we need HSM + audit logs for SOC2. do you have sample audit log schema?
01:21 Ethan: yes, we'll share the schema; note sometimes the downstream fields are labeled a bit differently in the export (eg. request_id vs reqId) — sorry transcription, I mean schema variants.
01:32 Priya: one thing we noticed — the SDK's function-calling helper throws on malformed structured output from the model once in a while, which cascades. any guardrails?
01:40 Ethan: yep, two approaches — 1) use the SDK's structured-output validator hook that will coerce known types and return a validation error rather than throwing, 2) implement a lightweight post-parse sanitizer. I'll attach the snippet.
01:52 Jamie: can you show the snippet now?
01:53 Ethan: yeah, quick paste — "// SDK example: callModel(..., {responseFormat:'json-schema', onValidate: validateFn})" — sorry the actual arg names vary by SDK version but gist is available.
02:07 Maya: note we bumped the SDK to 0.9.3 which fixes a retry bug with tool-call timeouts; some of you were on 0.9.1 in the POC.
02:17 Carlos: oh that might explain the intermittent timeouts we saw during the integration tests.
02:20 Jamie: yes we rolled the 0.9.1 locally. we'll upgrade.
02:24 Lina: about tool calling — we need confirmation that tools invoked (like our internal EHR lookup) do not leak PHI to logs or third-party telemetry.
02:33 Ethan: tools run in your network when using private deployment; in hosted mode Redwood logs request metadata for debugging but payloads can be redacted. for the POC in dedicated we can enable payload redaction and show you the redacted logs. the audit log table will show tool invocation times, tool name, request_id, but not the full patient text when redaction is on.
02:48 Priya: good. can you also confirm retention windows? we need 90-day log retention for staging and 365 for prod.
02:55 Maya: retention is configurable per environment; we'll send a docs link with default and custom retention options.
03:01 Jamie: back to results — we ran the structured output evaluation with our schema for discharge summaries. about 8% of responses fail strict schema validation, but 90% of those are fixable by the sanitizer.
03:14 Ethan: that's a good signal. can you share a few failing cases? often it's numbers formatted as strings or nested arrays collapsing.
03:22 Jamie: sending three examples in the shared drive link — note two of them have date formatting ambiguity, probably locale.
03:29 Carlos: on the cost side — what's the recommendation for lower unit cost? we saw token spend ramp up with open-ended completions.
03:36 Ethan: a couple levers: reduce max_tokens where possible, enforce structured output (so the model doesn't generate extra text), enable batching and caching for repeated prefixes, and try a quantized model variant. Redwood Optimize will give per-route recommendations.
03:49 Maya: also you can route lower criticality requests to a cheaper model variant for cost savings and failover to the high-quality variant on mismatch.
03:58 Lina: any impact to latency when using quantized models? last week's note said quantization reduces memory but can add ~10-20ms.
04:06 Ethan: depends on kernel selection, but in our tests quantized 4-bit on A100 reduced throughput CPU overhead and lowered p95. occasionally tail latency increased a bit for long sequences due to dequantization overhead, but overall cost wins often outweigh. we'll provide the exact bench matrices.
04:25 Jamie: regarding SDK integration: we tried the tool-call pattern where the model returns a tool name + args, and our service executes. the challenge we had is handling partial tool failures; how should we rollback?
04:36 Ethan: pattern we recommend is idempotent tool execution with compensating actions. the SDK's tool-call wrapper supports retry with exponential backoff and a dead-letter queue if you want manual intervention. also consider optimistic responses while tool runs async.
04:49 Carlos: would that affect auditability? we need traceability for every action.
04:52 Ethan: all tool calls get request_id and trace_id tags in logs; you can correlate across systems. with private deployment we can add additional headers too.
05:02 Jamie: quick note — Priya found an edge case where the function-call parser conflated two adjacent tool calls when the model output omitted separators.
05:11 Ethan: yeah that's a known tokenizer edge case; we pushed a heuristic to the SDK that enforces explicit JSON wrappers around tool calls. please upgrade SDK and enable strict parsing.
05:22 Maya: okay next steps — Ethan will upload the SDK sample and the sanitizer example; Jamie will run the quantized nightly; Lina will send security requirements.
05:31 Jamie: timeline looks good; we should have bench results by Monday.
05:34 Carlos: pricing — Maya you mentioned pilot pricing?
05:36 Maya: for the 3-month pilot on dedicated we can offer a committed seat + overage rate; I'll follow up with a spreadsheet.
05:43 Lina: and we need to see the KMS flow diagram for HSM integration before legal signs off.
05:48 Ethan: we'll attach the HSM flow and a sample key rotation policy.
05:53 Maya: any blockers we missed?
05:55 Priya: one small one — our infra team asked about autoscaling behavior during burst loads for the dedicated pool.
05:59 Ethan: dedicated supports configured autoscale and burst to shared capacity; we can provide expected cold-start times and recommended warm-up policies.
06:08 Maya: awesome. if no other items, we'll close and recap owners.
06:12 Carlos: that's it from product.
06:14 Jamie: good meeting, thanks.
